question: One US buyer borrowed at 9% in 1975, with 9% inflation; another at 4% in 2019, with 2%. Who paid more, really?
answer: The 2019 borrower. The real cost of a loan is its rate minus inflation. In 1975 the average 30-year mortgage charged about 9.05% while consumer prices rose about 9.1%: a real rate near zero. In 2019 it was 3.94% against 1.8% inflation, about 2% real. The 1975 debt melted as wages rose with prices.
move: Subtract inflation from any rate before calling it cheap or dear.
ask: When I compare a loan or a pay rise with the past, have I taken inflation out first?
trap: The 1975 borrower, because 9% looks more than twice 4%.
source: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey
